answer: Recurring compute bonds: each identity must re-earn its seat every epoch by solving a fresh, randomized task that burns real GPU time, and by locking a small bond that sits frozen like onyx until peers confirm its output is original. A farm of a thousand clones pays a thousand times the compute and bonds, so a gale of fake agents gets expensive fast. Near-duplicate wording and synced timing are a signal of one operator; flagged clusters lose their bonds. Since reward per seat stays below that cost, splitting one budget into many names never pays.
